definitions.gloss: jumble; hodgepodge; mishmash; all mixed together
definitions.explanation: A state where different things are mixed together in a disorderly way. Often implies a chaotic or haphazard combination without clear organization.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{出|だ}しの{中|なか}が{混|ま}ぜこぜだ。
examples.english: The inside of the drawer is all jumbled up.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}と{英語|えいご}が{混|ま}ぜこぜになっている。
examples.english: Japanese and English are all mixed together.

examples.japanese: {洗濯物|せんたくもの}を{色物|いろもの}と{白物|しろもの}を{混|ま}ぜこぜにして{洗|あら}ってしまった。
examples.english: I washed the laundry with colored and white items all mixed together.

notes:
An informal, colloquial word describing things mixed together in a disorderly way. Derives from {混|ま}ぜる (to mix).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {混|ま}ぜこぜになる: to become jumbled/mixed up
- {混|ま}ぜこぜにする: to mix up, to jumble together
- {混|ま}ぜこぜの{状態|じょうたい}: a jumbled state

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ごちゃ{混|ま}ぜ: jumbled mess (even more colloquial)
- ごちゃごちゃ: messy, cluttered (describes visual disorder)
- ちゃんぽん: mixed up, combined haphazardly (often for mixing drinks or languages)

USAGE:
Describes situations where different categories of things are mixed without order: languages ({日本語|にほんご}と{英語|えいご}が{混|ま}ぜこぜ), laundry items, drawer contents, etc. The nuance is mildly negative — things should ideally be sorted.

REGISTER:
Informal/colloquial. Not used in formal writing.
